vulnerabilities.description: Token and port injected into global window scope without validation. If injection point is compromised, authentication tokens are exposed. Tokens stored in window globals can be accessed by any script on the page.

User-generated announcement content (title/body) rendered without apparent sanitization. XSS risk if content contains malicious scripts. Affected: title and body fields from API responses displayed directly in UI.
Decision titles and content rendered from database without HTML escaping visible in code. User-controlled data from mission/prd/meeting contexts could contain XSS payloads.
Session state stored in plaintext localStorage, including session IDs and checkpoint revisions. localStorage is accessible to any script and persists across sessions. No encryption visible.
Error messages distinguish between 'user not found', 'invalid password', and other states. Allows attacker to enumerate valid email addresses via login/signup error messages.
CSS selector escaping uses custom implementation instead of native CSS.escape() in fallback path. Potential for selector injection if user-controlled data reaches cssId().
XMLSerializer output wrapped in encodeURIComponent without explicit XSS validation. If SVG content is user-controlled, data: URLs could bypass sanitization via Unicode/encoding tricks.
No visible Content-Security-Policy headers preventing inline script execution. Minified code makes CSP assessment incomplete.
Fallback ID generation uses Math.random() which is cryptographically weak. While crypto.randomUUID() is preferred first, fallback for legacy browsers is insufficient for security-sensitive IDs.
Numeric inputs parsed with Number() without range validation. Could allow negative budgets or extremely large values if validation is only frontend. Backend must enforce bounds.

recommendations: CRITICAL: Move TOKEN/PORT from window globals to secure storage (e.g., httpOnly cookies for tokens). Use postMessage API to communicate between frames if needed.
CRITICAL: Implement HTML entity encoding/sanitization for all user-generated content before rendering. Use a library like DOMPurify or React's built-in escaping consistently across panels.
CRITICAL: Encrypt sensitive session data in localStorage or migrate to sessionStorage + httpOnly cookies. Implement secure token storage without plaintext global access.
HIGH: Implement Content-Security-Policy header forbidding inline scripts. Use nonce-based script execution for browser injection.
HIGH: Align authentication error messages. Return generic 'Invalid credentials' for both invalid password and non-existent user to prevent email enumeration.
MEDIUM: Use native CSS.escape() consistently; audit custom cssId() fallback for injection via special characters.
MEDIUM: Validate SVG/XML inputs before serialization to data URLs; avoid user-controlled SVG content in screenshot generation.
MEDIUM: Add backend validation for budget caps, token limits, and numeric inputs (never trust frontend validation alone).
LOW: Document and enforce CSP policy in HTTP headers. Audit minified assets for hidden vulnerabilities via source map analysis.
LOW: Replace Math.random() fallback with crypto.getRandomValues() or upgrade minimum browser requirements to avoid weak RNG in IDs.
